title: Event Catalog Harmonizer: client-side capability detection and graceful schema fallbacks
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Motivation: As we evolve analytics payloads and introduce richer event types, clients (SDK/CLI/API callers) must be able to detect server-side capabilities and fall back to compatible envelopes without dropping high-value signals. This ticket implements the Event Catalog Harmonizer (ECH): a lightweight runtime service + client shims that publish capability predicates, validate outgoing events locally, and apply standardized fallback transforms when a feature gate is not available.
acceptance_criteria: ECH service exposes a /capabilities endpoint listing active event feature predicates and schema versions
SDKs and CLI consult /capabilities at startup and cache results with TTL and grace period
SDKs validate outgoing events against client-side generated tolerance rules and apply deterministic fallback transforms when required
Rolling upgrade playbook documented: canary on 5% of traffic, extend to 50%, then 100% with automated regressions checks
No increase in 95th percentile ingest latency by more than 50ms in canary; telemetry shows event fidelity differences per variant
Automated unit/integration tests covering three real event variants and a backfill simulation for older clients
work_items: Design ECH capability predicate format and low-entropy encoding
Implement ECH service with simple protobuf event catalog and JSON capability endpoint
Add capability caching + jittered refresh to SDK (python, js) and CLI
Build client-side validation library used by SDKs to detect incompatible fields and emit fallback events
Create a canary job in staging that replays historical traffic to validate no-loss fallback behavior
Instrument console dashboards: event-fidelity, fallback-rate, feature-gate-lag, client-version distribution
Author rollout/rollback runbook and automate canary promotion pipeline
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Old clients may silently drop fields leading to analytics skew. Mitigation: default to explicit fallback transforms that preserve core keys and emit 'schema_compat' flag
Risk: Increased client startup latency when fetching capabilities. Mitigation: TTL-based caching, use of ETag/If-Modified-Since and local bundled fallback catalog for first-call fast path
Risk: Backfill complexity for enriched events. Mitigation: backfill job templates and selective enrichment with provenance tags to enable deduplication
Risk: Security exposure from capability endpoint. Mitigation: endpoint is internal-only, authenticated using mTLS and KMS-signed tokens; security review required
testing_plan: Unit tests for capability parsing and fallback transforms
Integration tests: SDK <-> ECH with simulated schema flips
Load test: verify ECH scales to 10k concurrent client checks with <200ms 95th latency
Chaos test: simulate ECH intermittent failures, validate client degrade-to-bundled-fallback behavior
Rehearsal: staging run with 7 days of replayed production events and fidelity diff report
observability_requirements: Traces: end-to-end SDK event emission path tagged with client_version and used_catalog_version
Dashboards: per-model/route fallback heatmap and long-tail event losses
Alerts: fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m; capability_fetch_errors spike > 1% of requests
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy ECH to internal region, enable SDK bundling of local fallback catalog
Phase 1: canary 5% with automated smoke checks (ingest latency, fidelity diff) for 24h
Phase 2: expand to 50% with regression alerting for 48h
Phase 3: full rollout with scheduled backfill applied to historical events where safe
Rollback: flip SDK to 'bundled-only' mode via feature flag and revoke ECH capability token
